entries.title: Powerful number
entries.review_level: article scope; not an exhaustive literature audit
entries.target: Prove that no positive integer n has n, n+1, and n+2 all powerful, or supply a certified counterexample. Powerful means every prime divisor p occurs with p^2 dividing the integer.
entries.decision: Retain for target comparison; recent partial papers require review before selecting a subcase.
entries.obstruction: Known special-factorization arguments do not cover arbitrary squarefree parts. Arithmetic progressions consecutive in the ordered powerful-number sequence need not have common difference one.

entries.title: Siegel zero
entries.review_level: article scope; not an exhaustive literature audit
entries.target: Fix an exact uniform exceptional-real-zero-free region for primitive real Dirichlet L-functions, including constants and conductor range, then prove it or refute that statement.
entries.decision: Statement not yet fixed; defer until a concrete route justifies the analytic formalization cost.
entries.obstruction: A chosen numerical zero-free region is not automatically equivalent to the qualitative absence of Siegel zeros. Conditional implications from abc or GRH do not supply an unconditional solution.
